title: What is a closure?
description: A closure is a function that remembers its outer scope
example: function outer() { let x = 10; return function inner() { return x; } }
explanation: A closure is a function that retains access to variables from its enclosing scope even after the outer function has returned.
code: function createCounter() { let count = 0; return { increment: () => ++count }; }
code_explanation: The inner function retains access to count variable

title: Explain event delegation
description: Event delegation uses event bubbling to handle events at a parent level
explanation: Event delegation is a pattern where a single event listener is added to a parent element to handle events on its children using event bubbling.
code_explanation: Instead of adding listeners to each child we add one to the parent

title: What is the Virtual DOM?
description: The Virtual DOM is a lightweight copy of the actual DOM used by React
explanation: The Virtual DOM is an in-memory representation of the real DOM. React uses it to batch updates and minimize direct DOM manipulation for better performance.
code_explanation: React compares virtual DOM trees (diffing) and updates only changed parts

title: Explain useEffect hook
description: useEffect is a React hook for side effects in functional components
hints: Think about lifecycle methods in class components
explanation: useEffect runs after render and can handle side effects like API calls subscriptions and DOM updates. The dependency array controls when it re-runs.
code: useEffect(() => { const sub = api.subscribe(data => setData(data)); return () => sub.unsubscribe(); } [api]);
code_explanation: The cleanup function runs before the component unmounts or before the effect re-runs

title: What is SQL injection?
description: SQL injection is a code injection technique that exploits security vulnerabilities
example: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '' OR '1'='1'
explanation: SQL injection occurs when an attacker inserts malicious SQL code into a query through unsanitized input. Prevention includes parameterized queries and input validation.
code_explanation: Using parameterized queries prevents the input from being interpreted as SQL code

title: Explain JOIN types in SQL
description: SQL JOINs combine rows from two or more tables based on related columns
example: SELECT * FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
explanation: INNER JOIN returns matching rows. LEFT JOIN returns all left rows + matches. RIGHT JOIN returns all right rows + matches. FULL JOIN returns all rows from both.
code: SELECT e.name d.name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
code_explanation: LEFT JOIN ensures all employees appear even those without a department
